futures (live Yahoo feed) or indicative (group seed level).
The market this sister is, from `var('market_code')` — one value per warehouse.
The currency landed prices in this market are expressed in.
Every tracked commodity — the group catalog — with this market's facts beside it: the unit the local market quotes in and the duty in force today.
The MCX expiry calendar: every futures contract and option chain listed for the tracked codes, its commodity, lot and quote basis, days to expiry, and whether it traded in the latest session.
properties.grain: one MCX futures contract or option expiry chain

properties.description: Daily benchmark price per commodity in USD per quote unit, with day-on-day change, 20/50-day moving averages and a 252-trading-day range. Prices are non-additive: aggregate within one commodity only.

0 at the 52-week low, 1 at the high. Bounded by construction: the range is widened to include the close, because the feed ships candles whose high sits below their close (see assert_candles_bracket_the_close).
Close against the 50-day mean, as a share of that mean.
20-day mean above or below the 50-day. Null until both windows are full.
The day the regime turned, so a desk can act on the event rather than the state.
Standard deviations from the 60-day mean. Null until that window is full.
Annualised from 20 days of daily dispersion, on 252 trading days.
Against this commodity's own dispersion — 30% is calm for gas and extreme for rice.
A shortlist to look at, never a recommendation. Cheap and rising is accumulate; cheap and still falling returns hold, because the range signal alone cannot tell a bottom from a knife.

Timing signals on the USD benchmark — where a price sits in its own recent history, not what it costs. Every measure is unit-free, so unlike the price itself these are safe to compare across commodities.
Daily USD fixes (quote currency per 1 USD) with day-on-day change; the tracker's FX ticker.
The total the three contributions sum to, by construction.
Unsigned share of the rupee in the move, for ranking. Unsigned because the interesting case is a benchmark and a currency cancelling out, where the signed shares run past 1 and -1.
False for rows before the June 2026 verification (ADR-0001).

Why the landed rupee price moved over 20 trading days, split into the benchmark, the rupee and duty. An Indian buyer decides on landed rupees, and a USD-only signal cannot tell a commodity move from a currency move — which is the difference between a buying decision and a treasury one.
Units of this market's currency per 1 USD on the price date; 1 when the market prices in USD.
The import_duties row applied on this date.

Import landed price per commodity per day in this market's currency per its market unit: benchmark × USD/local × (1 + customs duty). The benchmark stands in for CIF value — freight, insurance, landing charges and local taxes are excluded. History before a tariff's `confirmed_from` uses today's rate; filter on `is_duty_rate_confirmed` when that matters. The same shape in every sister; `market_code` and `currency_code` say whose it is.
Garman–Klass (1980) OHLC range volatility over 30 sessions, annualised on 252.
Near-into-next roll yield to a long, annualised; negative in contango.

The continuous most-active MCX series per contract code with every trading metric: returns (1d–252d, YTD), SMA 20/50/200, EMA/MACD, RSI(14), ATR(14), Bollinger(20,2), 52-week range and drawdown, realised and Parkinson volatility, OI build-up across expiries, calendar spread, annualised carry, rollover, premium to landed import parity, and a legible stance. Indicators run on roll-free back-adjusted prices and are null until their window is full. Prices non-additive: aggregate within one contract_code.
properties.grain: one MCX contract code per trading day

properties.description: One session's Garman–Klass variance (not annualised).

The fact the per-commodity semantic model `mcx_commodities` reads.
properties.grain: one MCX commodity per trading day

properties.description: Traded value in rupees (MCX states it in ₹ lakh; × 100,000). Additive within a day.

futures, or indicative when the underlying has no live feed (zinc).
